research_insight_text_link.research_insight_description: LiliumX is engaged in the development of multivalent protein scaffolds for therapeutic applications, as described in 'Multivalent proteins and screening methods.' Their research focuses on multi-domain polypeptide constructs with multiple binding domains and a structural domain, supporting the identification of new therapeutic compounds. These activities align with the company’s emphasis on discovering bispecific antibodies against cancer using a protein technology platform.

overview_description.description: Valink Therapeutics researches multivalent and combinatorial target approaches intended to address treatment challenges in solid tumors and other therapeutic areas. Its work centers on identifying synergistic and less conventional target pairings and translating them into engineered biologic constructs with defined mechanisms of action. Valink Therapeutics operates as a therapeutics development organization that integrates antibody engineering, payload selection, and linker design within a single discovery framework.

product.name: LiliumX™ Universal Assembly Platform™
product.description: A modular platform that enables the rapid generation and screening of bispecific antibody-drug conjugates, multivalent multispecifics, or any combination thereof.

product.name: LiliumX™ Platform
product.description: A platform for rapid design and assembly of bispecific antibody-drug conjugates and other multifunctional biologics for cancer therapy.

product.name: Bispecific Antibody-Drug Conjugates (bsADCs)
product.description: Therapeutic molecules that target two cancer markers simultaneously to improve drug delivery and selectivity in cancer treatment.

product.name: Iterative Screening
product.description: A process that rapidly identifies potent drug candidates through iterative screening and design, leveraging a 1-day design process.

product.name: 5D Combinatorial Drug Discovery
product.description: A technology that combines components from proprietary format, binder, and payload libraries to construct drug candidates with bespoke geometries and target combinations.
